english.title: Attempt criminal damage to property - value under £5000
english.standardoffencewording:

english.notes:
Low value offences - where the value of the damage is below five thousand pounds, the offence can only be tried at a Magistrates Court. However, for all other purposes, it is still has the status of an 'either way offence'. It is possible to charge 'attempted criminal damage' of whatever value. For more on these issues, please see section 22 of the Magistrates' Court Act 1980.

(i) Property damaged/destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(ii) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iii) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth 1999).
(iv) There is no time limit on prosecution for this offence - even though only triable summarily it remains an either way offence.
